utterances.text: Before you -- yes, okay. Before you do that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: But what is your objection to Defence counsel's suggestion that -- MR. DI FAZIO: I have no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: That might help things. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. Yes. I have no objection to the witness briefly leaving.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So we have the usher leading the witness out, perhaps for as long as it will take to make the rearrangements, and then the witness will be led back into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honours, I think that Mr. Milan Simic should stay where he is because of his condition, but the other three can be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. So you can ask them to rearrange the way you would like them to be, without interfering with security arrangements, of course. So why don't you -- Mr. Pantelic, you can make suggestions who you want to sit where, without interfering with security.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The witness can come back.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I do like to apologise to the witness for this inconvenience.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. I'm sure he understands. Yes. The Prosecution can go ahead. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Mr. Lukac, I was asking you about Simo Zaric. Can you see him anywhere in this Court? If you can, please point him out.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC
utterances.text: The gentleman sitting at this first desk here, wearing glasses, in this first desk where the accused sit, I mean.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: I think, as my colleague Mr. Weiner points out, I think the record should indicate that Mr. Simo Zaric has been identified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And my next question is: Do you know a gentleman named Milan Simic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC
utterances.text: That is the gentleman in the wheelchair. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. Perhaps the record could also show that there's a correct identification there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And what about Blagoje Simic? Can you assist us with him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC
utterances.text: Mr. Blagoje Simic is sitting in the back row, and he has this short beard.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And what about Mr. Miroslav Tadic? Do you know him, and if so, can you indicate him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC
utterances.text: He is between Mr. Simic -- Blagoje Simic, and Mr. Milan Simic. MR. DI FAZIO: And I think if the record could indicate that the witness has correctly identified Mr. Tadic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, all the accused persons have been --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Her Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All the accused persons have been identified by the witness. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Mr. Simo Zaric, how long have you known him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC
utterances.text: Well, I've known Mr. Zaric since 1979.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Where did you first meet him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC
utterances.text: Bosanski Samac is a small town, and practically everybody knows everybody in that town. And Mr. Zaric, as far as I can remember, at the time was the manager of the furniture factory in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What's the name of the furniture factory?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC
utterances.text: It was Buducnost.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: When you met him, what was your occupation? What was your job at the time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC
utterances.text: At the time I was a political -- professional political advisor in the Council of Social and Political Organisations in the municipality of Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Now, you've told us that you met him when he was working at Buducnost. Did you know of him prior to that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC
utterances.text: Yes. I had heard about him prior to that, but I did not know him personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you know what his occupation was prior to his working at Buducnost?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC
utterances.text: I know that it was the secretary of the Secretariat of the Interior of the municipality of Bosanski Samac before becoming the manager of this furniture factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Is there any simpler way of putting "secretary of the Secretariat of the Interior of the municipality of Bosanski Samac"? What sort of position is that in common parlance?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC
utterances.text: Yes. Simply, he was the chief of the SUP, chief of police.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. I appreciate your attention to detail, but unless specifically asked, I think when you're describing this position, if we could just use "chief of police." It's a lot easier for us all. Now, do you know what period of time he was chief of police, I mean in the period of time prior to Buducnost?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure, but between 1974 and 1978, I'd say. That was the period. Within that time framework.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. How long was he associated with Buducnost?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC
utterances.text: I think that Mr. Zaric was its manager between 1978 and sometime in 1981, perhaps early 1982.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did he -- in carrying out his duties with Buducnost, did he remain in Bosanski Samac throughout that period of time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC
utterances.text: Well, he held -- he was the manager, yes, of that factory in Bosanski Samac, and that is where he lived.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did he ever go to Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC
utterances.text: And after that, Mr. Zaric, from the office of the manager of Buducnost, moved over, I think, to the office of that same processing industry in Belgrade, and I think that he spent about a year in that office.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And is it the case -- I just want to be clear. I'm not suggesting that this is correct or not, but was the period of time that he was in Belgrade sometime during that period between 1978 and 1981 or 1982? Was it during that period of time that he was in Belgrade for a year, or was it in some other period of time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC
utterances.text: No. It was after 1981. So I think that it was 1982, most likely.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did he eventually return to Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC
utterances.text: He did, in '80 -- I think early 1983.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What did he do upon his return to Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC
utterances.text: Upon his return, Mr. Zaric began to work for the State Security Service in Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: I want you to explain to the Chamber what precisely the State Security Service was in the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC
utterances.text: I have never been on the staff of that service, but as I understand it, this is the intelligence service, the Civilian Intelligence Service in the former Yugoslavia. Civilian, I mean, because of course the army had its own intelligence service, so there was a separate Military Intelligence Service and this one was civilian.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did it, like the MUP or the SUP or the TO, have its own acronym?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC
utterances.text: Yes, SDB [Realtime transcript read in error "SDP"], which means sluzba drzavne bezbednosti, State Security Service.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: SDB, not "P." SDB. That would be correct. MR. DI FAZIO: I'm very grateful --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sure the Prosecution has seen that. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. I'm very grateful to my learned friend for that illumination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Now, as an intelligence service, what sort of brief did it have? What sort of responsibilities did it carry out, as far as you're aware?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC
utterances.text: The service of that agency was engaged in the collection of intelligence information about individuals and events that could jeopardise the system of the then Yugoslavia, or rather, in the republics, members of the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you ever have any professional dealings with the SDB as a police officer? I'm not talking about Mr. Simo Zaric, but just generally, did the police ever liaise or have any professional dealings?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC
utterances.text: Well, yes. There were contacts from time to time, but it happened very seldom.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Was there an exchange of information between the police and the SDB?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't say so. That is, I wouldn't call it that. I wouldn't call it exchange. Rather, I'd say that the SDB from time to time used some information or some intelligence about individuals or events obtained by the other police, by the public police.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Do I take it from your answer that as far as the intelligence flows were concerned, it was one-way traffic, police to SDB?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Now, getting back to Mr. Simo Zaric. You said that he obtained a position with the SDB. Where was he based?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC
utterances.text: In Doboj. Doboj is a town, a municipality. At that time, Doboj was the regional centre at the time, covering the ten municipalities in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Can I just ask to you pause there? MR. DI FAZIO: Perhaps at this stage it would be a good idea for us to refer to the Times map, which is the large map behind me. If it could be placed on the easel, it might make it easier for the rest -- the remainder of this witness's evidence. And that map is Exhibit -- for the purposes of the transcript, it's P15. I'm sorry. The usher has produced a map of Bosanski Samac, but the Times map of the former Yugoslavia, the large map of the former Yugoslavia. Thank you. I'm grateful to the courtroom staff. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Can you just point out on the large map where Doboj is, please?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC
utterances.text: It's here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much. And perhaps if you'd resume your seat now. MR. DI FAZIO: And could I also produce to the witness Exhibit P12, which is a rough map of the municipality, and that could be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And could you please point out to the Chamber where it appears on that map so that they can see it -- the members of the Chamber can see it in more perspective?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC
utterances.text: It's here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. I have no further need of the map. Now, you said that the -- he was based in Doboj. Did the SDB have any headquarters in the region?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC
utterances.text: The SDB didn't have headquarters, it had a centre. That's what it was called, the Centre of the State Security Service for the Region of Doboj, with its seat in Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Can you comment on the geographical structure of the SDB, if any?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC
utterances.text: You mean the organigram, how that service was organised in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: No, just the -- let me withdraw the question. Let me ask you this: Did the centre in Doboj cover a certain area?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC
utterances.text: Well, I said that this centre covered ten municipalities. The centre also had its detached offices in these ten municipalities. So that, for instance, for Bosanski Samac municipality, the seat of this detached office was in the neighbouring municipality of Modrica, so that this detached office covered three municipalities, the municipality -- the Bosanski Samac and Modrica and Odzak, all three of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Do you know precisely what Mr. Simo Zaric's role was in Doboj? If you don't, say so.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC
utterances.text: I think that during his assignment in Doboj, he was an operative officer, an agent of that service. And after that, I think sometime in late 1985, he came to head this detached office in Modrica.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: How long did he remain in that position?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC
utterances.text: He remained in that position as the head of the detached office, so from the time he took it up. And I think it was the latter half of late 1985 until September or October 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What happened in September or October 1991?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC
utterances.text: As far as I know, Mr. Zaric was then retired. He retired.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Throughout that period of time, the late 1980s and into September or October of 1991, did he reside in Bosanski Samac or elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC
utterances.text: He lived in Bosanski Samac and then commuted to Modrica, to the adjacent municipality, because that is where his detached office was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: May I ask you some questions about the man you've identified as Blagoje Simic? How long have you known him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly when he started his physician's practice in Bosanski Samac, but it could have been sometime in early -- in the beginning of the 1990s. That is, I met him before the war. I've known him before the war for some seven or eight years. That would be roughly that period of time. And he worked as a physician in the health centre in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Before we continue with Mr. Blagoje Simic, I should just briefly return to Mr. Simo Zaric. You've told us about his work. Did you ever have any social contact with him at all? Anything at all?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC
utterances.text: Possibly, but I really can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And now if we can return to Mr. Blagoje Simic. In the seven or eight years that you knew him, what was the nature of your relationship? Was it professional? Were you friends? How would you describe it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC
utterances.text: Well, we lived in the same town, so we knew one another. We were acquaintances there. On the other hand, possibly within the framework of my work, I may have contacted with him because he was a physician in the health centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Were you aware of his undertaking any political activities?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, at that time, Mr. Blagoje Simic was not politically active.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And what about after that time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC
utterances.text: I think he began in 1990 when the Serb Democratic Party was formed. And as far as I know, he was elected the president of that party for Bosanski Samac, and I believe that his political activity, political commitment, began then.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: I want to ask you a general question. Did your activities as police chief ever bring you into contact with him as a result of his political connections, political activities? For example, did you attend meetings, that sort of thing?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC
utterances.text: I think that we both attended the same meeting three or four times. Different roles: I would be representing police at those meetings, and Mr. Simic as the president of that party and later on as the Vice-President of the Municipal Assembly of Bosanski Samac, because after the multi-party elections, Mr. Blagoje Simic was appointed the Vice-President of the Municipal Assembly of Bosanski Samac, as far as I remember. It was not a professional assignment. He was a volunteer.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Have you any idea about when he received that appointment?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC
utterances.text: He was appointed after the multi-party elections and after the new Municipal Assembly was formed, so that should be the beginning of 1991. As far as I've said, as my -- if my memory serves me well, because, after all, it was ten years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did he retain that position in April of 1992? Did he still have that position?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC
utterances.text: Yes, he did. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I note the time. Do you wish me to proceed, or would this be an appropriate moment to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, this is the appropriate moment to break and adjourn the proceedings to Monday, at 9.30 hours. I do hope that by next week we shall have the facilities required by Mr. Milan Simic so that we can use the afternoons as well so that the trial can move much faster. Yes, Mr. Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may, just a short issue, actually a little issue. We have requested from the Registry to be provided and supplied by the copies of audiotapes and videotapes of the proceedings, and our basis was we have to give our observation to the transcript in a week or eight days - I don't know. We cannot act without these things. We cannot simply read the rough version of the transcript and then to give our objections or submissions. With regard to the videotapes, the Defence has certain, I would say, methods for - based on the science, of course, forensic science - with regard to the analysis of the witness behaviour, or witness behaviour before the Court, and then we are trying to establish certain standards, whether the witness is speaking true or not, et cetera. And we have been informed by Mr. Marc Dubuisson that we cannot be provided with videotapes, which is really surprising me because these are the open sessions, nothing to hide. These sessions are broadcasting to various countries and systems, and really I'm a little bit surprised. And we as Defence are blocked now, because it was almost two weeks that we are in all these proceedings and we do not have any audio or videotape, and we are in problem because this burden will be getting more and more each day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So I kindly ask - and I can even formulate my motion or application to this Trial Chamber - that the Registry or Court Management be directed to provide us all this materials, of course subject to all restrictions or other terms, of course. I don't know what is the situation here. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber will be able to ask the Registrar and will be able to find out what the problem is or whether facilities can be made available, and then the Trial Chamber will be able to inform the Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honours, for raising this issue, because we filed our application and it was denied. It was refused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: By the Registrar?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: By the Registrar, by Mr. Dubuisson, or I don't know who is in charge. It was refused, and now I'm getting to the upper levels. That's a matter of our proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So you're in fact appealing against that refusal?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That would be the case, of course, in the interests of justice, for the Article 20, 21 of the Statute, rights of the defendants, European Convention of Human Rights, et cetera, et cetera, all these general principles of law. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Trial Chamber was just discussing the matter. We will find out from the Registry and also with the Prosecution, and we will be able to give an answer probably before the end of next week.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm much obliged, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Any other matters? The proceedings will adjourn, and we will continue on Monday at 9.30 a.m.. The Court will rise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
